episodes.193798: An upper level shortwave trough approached from the north, with the region in the front left quadrant of an upper level jet streak. With warm, humid air at the surface, SBCAPE values were able to climb to around 2000 J/kg. Storms fired up and some were able to become strong to severe and produce damaging wind gusts.
episodes.193815: Various social media posts regarding a waterspout just offshore Port Aransas.
episodes.193869: Thunderstorms developed near a cold front in Minnesota then tracked eastward through Wisconsin during late evening hours on Monday (8/26) into the early morning hours of Tuesday (8/27).  The strongest storms produced damaging winds across northeast Wisconsin.
episodes.193870: Thunderstorms produced strong winds over the bay of Green Bay during the late evening hours on Monday (8/26) into the early morning hours on Tuesday (8/27).
episodes.193872: A line of thunderstorms developed along an outflow boundary during the morning hours on Tuesday (8/27) and tracked through central and east-central Wisconsin during the late morning and early afternoon hours.  The strongest storms produced damaging winds as they tracked through the area.
episodes.193877: Thunderstorms produced strong winds over the bay of Green Bay and Lake Michigan during the late morning and early afternoon hours on Tuesday (8/27).
episodes.194080: Scattered thunderstorms developed over southwest Nebraska and western Kansas during the late afternoon hours of August 26th, then shifted east-northeast during the evening hours along the resultant outflow boundary. The vast majority of this activity was only loosely organized due to generally weak deep layer wind shear. However, a couple severe wind gusts in the 60-65 MPH range were observed by mesonets in Buffalo County between 9-10PM CDT. No additional severe weather occurred with this event as a broad shield of rain and embedded weak storms continued eastward across the remainder of south central Nebraska into the overnight.
episodes.194166: Storms developed across Minnesota during the afternoon hours of the 26th across Minnesota and moved into northwest Wisconsin during the evening hours. These storms were mainly wind producing storms with numerous reports of downed trees and power lines across the region. Minor flash flooding was also observed in Siren.
episodes.194167: A decaying complex of storms moved northeast out of east-central Minnesota in the hours after sunrise the morning of the 27th. A few isolated reports of tree damage were received along with a few washed out gravel roads from the heavy rainfall.
episodes.194193: Multiple lines of thunderstorms developed ahead and along a cold front. The first line of stronger thunderstorms worked their way down across northeast WI and over Lake Michigan overnight into the morning of August 27. An Additional line of stronger thunderstorms followed a similar track through the late morning hours and early afternoon of the 27th.
episodes.194223: Showers and thunderstorms developed late in the day on Aug 27th in northeast Missouri and spread into southeast Iowa and far western Illinois into the evening. Large hail up to golf ball size fell for nearly one half hour straight in Rutledge, MO.||A pronounced downburst (powerful winds that descend from a thunderstorm and spread out quickly once they hit the ground) caused widespread damage in Burlington, IA, knocking down trees, limbs, and powerlines. Five homes had holes in the roofs due to falling limbs. A commercial storage building had a partial roof collapse and another large tall outbuilding had partial roofing peeled back, consistent with wind estimates of at least 80 mph. ||Rainfall totals of 2 to 4 inches were observed in parts of northeast Missouri and southeast Iowa. ||Oppressive heat and humidity that began on the 26th and persisted into the 27th helped spawn these storms. Both Dubuque (tied) and Moline (exceeded) daily record highs on the 27th, with Moline reaching 98�� and Dubuque 94��.
episodes.194248: Scattered severe storms developed during the afternoon and early evening across eastern Kansas, producing wind gusts up to 60 mph and hail up to half dollar size.  Flooding was also reported in Jefferson county.
episodes.194505: Numerous thunderstorms developed across the area resulting in wind gusts of 60-66 mph. Wind damage was also reported in eastern Gove county near Quinter.
episodes.194600: A line of strong thunderstorms ahead of a cold front produced straight line winds and some tree and power line damage in southeast WI.
episodes.194716: Lingering high moisture with PWATs near 2 inches across NE FL produced locally heavy rainfall in diurnally enhanced afternoon showers and isolated storms.
episodes.194740: A small cluster of thunderstorms raced across southern Lake Michigan and came onshore, causing extensive tree damage.
episodes.194741: Penny size hail was reported from a thunderstorm that moved through northwest Ohio.
episodes.194742: A small cluster of thunderstorms raced across southern Lake Michigan and came onshore, causing extensive tree damage from Michigan City northeast to Union Pier MI and then weakened with inland extent.
episodes.194822: A line of severe thunderstorms developed as they moved into southwest South Dakota. These storms produced wind gusts to over 70 mph, along with embedded areas of hail, as they tracked through southwest and south-central South Dakota.
episodes.195028: A couple disturbances crossed the Upper Great Lakes, driving a couple rounds of storms...one in the early morning hours which crossed Lake Michigan, and a second round that developed around midday on the 27th, crossing northern Michigan and resulting in areas of wind damage from Lake Michigan to near Saginaw Bay.
episodes.195123: Scattered thunderstorms, spurred by a ridge-rider mid-level wave across North Dakota,  formed generally near a weak surface convergence boundary across far northern Nebraska and southeast South Dakota and a surface front over central and northeastern South Dakota. The storms weakened before moving too far eastward due to a strong thermal cap, but this warm and drier layer allowed storms to briefly produce some stronger winds east of the James River.
episodes.195155: A complex of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of August 26, and grew upscale into a line of storms that produced widespread wind damage across central and eastern Minnesota. There were likely hundreds, if not thousands of trees damaged across the Twin Cities metro area.
episodes.195160: A line of thunderstorms lifted up from the southwest during the early morning hours of August 27. This caused widespread wind damage across far eastern Minnesota, including some wind damage to the MN State Fair.
episodes.195161: A line of thunderstorms moved from eastern Minnesota into western Wisconsin during the early morning hours of August 27. This caused some spots of wind damage in western Wisconsin.
episodes.195550: Temperatures climbing into the low to mid 90s with dew points in the low to mid 70s Tuesday afternoon lead to heat indices reaching around 100 degrees across most of southeast Michigan. This hot and humid airmass fueled an expanding line of strong to severe thunderstorms which moved through southeast Michigan just before 4 PM and 7 PM. Wind gusts of 40-65 MPH impacted the majority of southeast Michigan, downing tree limbs and trees. Isolated stronger gusts between 66-76 mph were also observed across the Detroit Metro Area. In total, about 380,000 customers lost power in Michigan, with around 210,000 in the DTE service area/southeast Michigan region. Just about every county in southeast Michigan experienced at least minor tree damage. Due to the rapid movement of the line of thunderstorms, rainfall totals were limited to under 1 inch across the majority of the area. Much heavier rainfall occurred with thunderstorms moving through Washtenaw and Wayne counties Tuesday night, leading to total rainfall totals around 3 inches in Ann Arbor.
episodes.195578: Building instability ahead of passing cold front produced a bowing line of severe thunderstorms in the early morning of the 27th.  Power outages and sporadic tree and power line damage were reported across portions of central Upper Michigan from the storms.
episodes.195730: During the evening of the 27th, a complex of severe thunderstorms impacted northern and northeast Illinois producing widespread wind damage, mostly to trees and power lines, as well as several instances of severe hail.
episodes.195741: Thunderstorms moving through Lake St. Clair, Detroit River, and Lake St. Clair River produced wind gusts up to 50 knots.
episodes.195742: Thunderstorms moving through southern Lake Huron and Saginaw Bay produced wind gusts in excess of 50 knots.
episodes.195757: Building instability ahead of a cold front moving through the area produced scattered strong to severe thunderstorms over portions of Lake Superior during the early morning of the 27th.
episodes.195769: Instability ahead of a passing cold front generated strong thunderstorms over the Bay of Green Bay in the early morning of the 27th.
episodes.196024: A lone supercell thunderstorm developed over eastern Brown county during the mid afternoon hours of August 26th. As this storm migrated slowly east, it grew upscale producing very large hail along a swath form south of Bassett to the O'Neill and Inman areas. Hail up to 4 inches in diameter was reported, along with numerous reports of 2 to 3 inch diameter hail.
episodes.196028: A complex of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of August 26 across central Minnesota, and grew upscale into a line of storms that produced widespread wind damage across western Wisconsin during the evening.
episodes.196038: There were numerous reports of damaging wind gusts as well as a few reports of large hail on August 27th.  At one point over three hundred thousand people were left without power across southern lower Michigan. Numerous trees, tree limbs and power lines were blown down.  There was also one injury when a tree fell onto a house in St. John's.
episodes.196044: During the evening hours on August 26th, a line of thunderstorms produced isolated wind damage in Buffalo County when trees fell onto power lines in Mondovi.
episodes.196159: An isolated thunderstorm brought report of low end wind damage.
episodes.196231: During the afternoon and evening hours of August 27th, storms brought large hail and damaging wind gusts to portions of Missouri.
episodes.196282: Locally induced afternoon thunderstorms over western Puerto Rico led to rockfall and mudslides.
episodes.196348: Evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce a strong marine wind gust in the Tampa Bay area.
episodes.199143: A surface cold front drifted southeastward across southwestern QC, the central Great Lakes, and southern WI during the early evening of the 27th through the very early morning of the 28th. Within the warm and humid sector ahead of the cold front, a line of multicell thunderstorms persisted east-southeastward across Lake Erie during the evening of the 27th and generated periodic gale-force peak convective wind gusts along the northern OH and northwest PA shore. During the early morning of the 28th, a separate cluster of multicell thunderstorms persisted east-southeastward over western Lake Erie and produced a gale-force peak convective wind gust at the Toledo Harbor Light C-MAN Station. These storms occurred in an ambient environment with weak to moderate MUCAPE, moderate to strong DCAPE, and moderate effective bulk shear.
episodes.200448: A surface cold front drifted southeastward across southwestern QC, the central Great Lakes, and southern WI during the early evening of the 27th through the very early morning of the 28th. Within the warm and humid sector ahead of the cold front, a line of multicell thunderstorms persisted east-southeastward across northwest OH and produced sporadic straight-line convective wind damage and measured severe straight-line convective wind gusts. These storms occurred in an ambient environment with weak to moderate MUCAPE, moderate to strong DCAPE, and moderate effective bulk shear.
